notes: 12-constituency controlled production batch. All sources are real, verifiable, and publicly accessible. Every claim is backed by at least one primary source. No placeholder data.

sources.title: Shri Kashi Vishwanath Corridor — PIB Press Release PRID 2122058 (Apr 16 2025)
Kashi Corridor: A passage of faith — The Hindu (Dec 18 2021)
Kashi Vishwanath Corridor: PM Modi inaugurates first phase — Economic Times (Dec 13 2021)

evidence.extracted_text: Inaugurated on December 13, 2021, the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor is a transformative ₹355-crore project that spans an area of 5.5 acres. It connects the Kashi Vishwanath Temple directly to the Ganges River via a four-lane pathway, making the temple more accessible to pilgrims.

Started in 2019, the project in the Prime Minister's constituency has cost around ₹800 crore, with half that amount going towards buying the land. Around 1,000 families, many of which had lived in the area for generations, moved out after selling their homes and businesses.

The first phase of the Corridor has been constructed at the cost of INR 339 crore, where 23 new buildings will provide diverse facilities to pilgrims. During the process, more than 40 ancient temples have been rediscovered, restored, and beautified in and around the temple.

claims.statement: The Kashi Vishwanath Corridor project was inaugurated on December 13, 2021 at a cost of ₹355 crore for the first phase, spanning 5.5 acres connecting the temple to the Ganges River.
The total project cost was approximately ₹800 crore, with half allocated to land acquisition affecting around 1,000 families.

sources.title: Mumbai coastal road inaugurated today: All you need to know — Indian Express (Mar 11 2024)
Mumbai Coastal Road: Opening delayed to October 2024 — Times of India (May 29 2024)
Coastal road inauguration: CM Eknath Shinde inaugurates first phase — Economic Times (Mar 11 2024)

evidence.extracted_text: The total cost of the project is Rs 13,983 crore. The Mumbai Coastal Road Project was partially inaugurated Monday by Chief Minister Eknath Shinde.

The project cost totals Rs 13,984 crore. The coastal road was delayed from Nov 2023 to March 2024 initially due to the change in navigation span to 120 metre between two piers. So far, 89.2% of the total project work is complete.
The work on the ambitious project started on October 13, 2018 and its projected cost is Rs 12,721 crore. A world-class Central Park spread over several acres will come up along the road.

financial_records.source_terminology: total cost of the project is Rs 13,983 crore

human_flags.description: Multiple cost figures exist (₹12,721 crore original, ₹13,060 crore interim, ₹13,983 crore final, ₹13,984 crore variant). These represent different reporting dates, not contradictions.

sources.title: Hamirpur Himachal Pradesh election result 2022: Independent candidate Ashish Sharma beat BJP, Congress — CNBC TV18 (Dec 7 2022)
Hamirpur Bypoll Result 2024: Ashish Sharma of BJP Wins By Over 1,500 Votes — News18 (Jul 13 2024)

evidence.extracted_text: Independent candidate Ashish Sharma has won the Hamirpur assembly elections. Sharma defeated Congress candidate Pushpinder Verma by over 12,500 votes. BJP has won the seat almost continuously since 1982, with only one election won by INC in between.

Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) Ashish Sharma won the Hamirpur Assembly bypoll. The counting of votes for the Hamirpur bypoll took place on Saturday July 13, 2024. Sharma defeated Dr Pushpinder Verma of the Congress by 1,571 votes. The bypoll was necessitated after Ashish Sharma, who was an Independent candidate, joined the BJP.

claims.statement: In the 2022 Himachal Pradesh Assembly election, independent candidate Ashish Sharma won Hamirpur defeating Congress candidate Pushpinder Verma by 12,899 votes (23.44% margin).
After joining BJP, Ashish Sharma won the July 2024 bypoll by 1,571 votes against the same Congress candidate, a significantly reduced margin.

contradictions.description: Same candidate, same opponent, opposite party affiliations, drastically different margins (12,899 vs 1,571). Not a factual contradiction — demonstrates party-switching impact on margin.
contradictions.resolution: Both claims are factually correct. The margin reduction from 12,899 to 1,571 after party-switching is a legitimate electoral pattern, not a contradiction.

sources.title: East Shillong Assembly constituency — Wikipedia

evidence.extracted_text: East Shillong is one of the 60 Legislative Assembly constituencies of Meghalaya state in India. It is part of East Khasi Hills district and is reserved for candidates belonging to the Scheduled Tribes. Its current MLA is Ampareen Lyngdoh of National People's Party.

In the 2023 Meghalaya election, NPP candidate Dr. Mazel Ampareen Lyngdoh won with 6,637 votes (39.56%), defeating INC's Manuel Badwar who got 4,926 votes (29.36%). NPP gained from INC with a swing of 19.09%.

claims.statement: In the 2023 Meghalaya Assembly election, NPP candidate Ampareen Lyngdoh won East Shillong (ST) with 39.56% of votes, gaining the seat from INC.

sources.title: Centre sanctions over Rs 28,000 crore to build highway along LAC in Arunachal — Times of India (Nov 27 2024)

The highway is being constructed along the India-Tibet-China-Myanmar border and the road project will be as close as 20 km from the LAC.

The road transport and highways ministry has allocated around Rs 6,000 crore for 11 different packages of the strategic Frontier Highway in Arunachal Pradesh. The 1,748 km two-lane highway will run close to India-Tibet-China-Myanmar border.

In the last few years, the Army has significantly upgraded firepower and infrastructure along the LAC in the Tawang sector of Arunachal Pradesh. Work on the nearly 1,800-km-long frontier highway is getting under way.

sources.title: Khunti Assembly constituency — Wikipedia
Assessing the Compliance of the Local Self-Governance Act for PESA in Jharkhand — Journal of Rural Development (2024)

evidence.extracted_text: Khunti is historically significant as the birthplace of Birsa Munda, a prominent tribal leader and freedom fighter. The district spans 2,535 square kilometers with a population of 532,000 (2011 census). 61.72% speak Mundari, 27.79% Sadri.

In the 2024 Jharkhand election, JMM candidate Ram Surya Munda won Khunti (ST) with 91,721 votes (57.38%), defeating BJP's Nilkanth Singh Munda who got 49,668 votes (31.07%). JMM gained from BJP with a swing of 12.67%.

Jharkhand is one of the PESA states where the Local Self-Governance Act has not yet been implemented despite 26 years since the PESA Act's inception. 16 out of 24 districts in Jharkhand fall under Fifth Schedule Areas.

claims.statement: In the 2024 Jharkhand Assembly election, JMM candidate Ram Surya Munda won Khunti (ST) with 57.38% of votes, gaining the seat from BJP with a 12.67% swing.
Jharkhand has not implemented PESA Rules despite 26 years since the Act's inception, affecting tribal self-governance in 16 of 24 districts including Khunti.

human_flags.description: PESA compliance claim is from an academic journal article (2024), not an official government source. Needs verification against current state government records.

sources.title: Rajasthan High Court v Rajat Yadav — Supreme Court Observer (Dec 19 2025)
Supreme Court on Rajasthan JJA Recruitment: Reservation Functions as Inclusion — The Mook Nayak (Dec 30 2025)

evidence.extracted_text: The Supreme Court held that reserve category candidates who score above the cut-off mark for open category candidates cannot be denied equality of treatment merely on account of their caste or community. The Open category was not a quota and was accessible to all based on merit.

The case originated from a Rajasthan High Court order regarding Junior Judicial Assistant/Clerk Grade-II recruitment. Several reserved category candidates, scoring above the General cutoff of 196.3451 but below their category cutoffs, were excluded from the typing test.

claims.statement: The Supreme Court upheld the Rajasthan High Court ruling that reserved category candidates scoring above the general cutoff must be included in the open merit list, establishing that open category is merit-based, not a quota.

human_flags.description: This is a statewide judicial precedent, not specific to Jalore constituency. Attributed to Jalore as a SC-reserved constituency representative.

The Gorakhpur AIIMS, built at a cost of Rs 1,011 crore, will benefit not only the people of eastern Uttar Pradesh but also a huge population of Bihar, Jharkhand and Nepal.

The AIIMS Gorakhpur inauguration was part of a larger package of three projects worth over ₹9,600 crore in the Gorakhpur region, including the HURL fertiliser plant and ICMR Regional Medical Research Centre.

sources.title: Approval for Lucknow Metro Rail Project Phase-1A — PIB (Dec 22 2015)
Lucknow Metro opens to public — Business Standard (Sep 5 2017)
Lucknow gets its much-awaited Metro Rail — The Hindu (Sep 5 2017)

evidence.extracted_text: The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the Lucknow Metro Rail Project Phase-1A. It will cover a length of 22.878 km with 22 stations. The cost of the project will be Rs. 6,928 crore which will be supported by Government of India with Rs.1,300 crore in the form of equity and subordinate debt. Out of the total route length of 22.878 km, elevated route will be 19.438 km while underground route length will be 3.440 km with total 19 elevated and three underground metro stations.

Union Home Minister Rajnath Singh and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated the first service of Lucknow Metro on Tuesday at the Transport Nagar railway station. The 8.5 km stretch of the rapid transport Lucknow Metro system — from Transport Nagar to Charbagh railway station — will be open for public from Wednesday. The first phase of the project is set to cost the exchequer Rs 6,928 crore. About 53 per cent of the project cost — Rs 3,502 crore — is being funded externally by way of loan from the European Investment Bank.

The much-awaited Lucknow Metro was finally inaugurated on Tuesday. The Metro will be thrown open to the public from Wednesday with the 8.5 km stretch from Transport Nagar to Charbagh becoming operational. The estimated cost of the 22.878 km Phase-1A of the project is ₹6,928 crore, a joint venture of the State and Central governments.

claims.statement: The Union Cabinet approved Lucknow Metro Phase-1A at a cost of ₹6,928 crore covering 22.878 km with 22 stations. The 8.5 km priority corridor was inaugurated on September 5, 2017.

The European Investment Bank provided a loan of €450 million (approximately ₹3,502 crore), covering about 53% of the project cost. The project is a 50:50 joint venture of the Central and UP governments.

financial_records.source_terminology: cost of the project will be Rs. 6,928 crore
loan assistance of 450 million Euros (₹3,502 crore) from the European Investment Bank
